agency: Oklahoma Highway Patrol (Oklahoma Department of Public Safety)
outcome_detail: Federal civil rights suit (42 U.S.C. 1983) filed October 23, 2025 in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Oklahoma (Harrington v. Evans et al, 5:25-cv-01260) naming Jarquez Evans, the Oklahoma Highway Patrol and the Oklahoma Department of Public Safety; Evans was served in February 2026 as he left his preliminary hearing. No settlement, judgment or dismissal reported as of July 2026.
criminal_detail: Evans was arrested March 28, 2025 and charged in Oklahoma County with first-degree rape and forcible oral sodomy; OSBI analysis reportedly matched his DNA to a semen stain on his uniform pants. He was bound over for trial on February 18, 2026, pleaded not guilty at his April 29, 2026 formal arraignment, and the case was set for a pretrial conference in August 2026. No trial verdict reported as of July 2026.
incident_date_approx: January 26, 2025 (traffic stop near SE 29th Street and S High Avenue, Oklahoma City)
description: A woman filed a civil lawsuit against former Oklahoma Highway Patrol trooper Jarquez Evans, the Oklahoma Highway Patrol and the Oklahoma Department of Public Safety after a January 26, 2025 traffic stop in southeast Oklahoma City. According to the criminal complaint and reporting, Evans pulled the woman over for an expired tag, told her she could follow him down the street or go to jail, got into her car, and then allegedly forced her to perform a sex act and raped her. Evans was fired, arrested in March 2025, and charged with first-degree rape and forcible oral sodomy; he has pleaded not guilty and was bound over for trial in February 2026. The federal civil suit, filed in October 2025 in the Western District of Oklahoma, remains pending alongside the criminal case.
notes: Civil suit was served on Evans as he left the courthouse following his February 2026 preliminary hearing, per local reporting.
